subject: Service resilience addendum request — Quantum Health (order form exhibit)
messages:
From: Samir Desai <samir.desai@quantumhealth.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Cc: anna.kowalski@quantumhealth.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service resilience addendum — initial ask

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this. As we move toward signature on the MSA + Order Form, our security and procurement teams have asked for a short availability/resilience rider that captures:

- Target regional uptime (99.95%) and exception carve-outs for scheduled maintenance windows and force majeure.
- A regional failover commitment and an outlined fallback model (what counts as an approved fallback replica).
- Clarified latency SLOs for the 95th percentile for API calls (standard vs. burst).
- A brief escalation & notification timeline for multi-region incidents.

We do not expect full SLA credits language up front, but we need an exhibit that can be attached to the Order Form and the MSA covering the above so our legal/procurement can review.

Can you send an initial rider draft and a suggested order-form exhibit paragraph we can present to our CFO and legal? Ideally by end of week — our procurement window is tight.

I've attached the procurement checklist we usually circulate (see attachment: QH_Procurement_Checklist.pdf).

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Desai
Head of Procurement, Quantum Health
samir.desai@quantumhealth.com

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear ask and the checklist. Looping in Rishi and David for technical / ops language and to confirm what we can commit to in the Order Form exhibit.

High level next steps from my side:
- We will send an initial rider draft (word) and a PDF redline for the Order Form exhibit by EOW.
- Rishi will propose concrete percentile/latency numbers and carve-outs for scheduled maintenance.
- David will propose the operational notification cadence and ownership for incident escalations.

A couple of clarifying Qs so we can tune the draft:
1) Do you need region-specific uptime numbers (e.g., US-East vs EU-West) or a single global SLA?
2) For failover, do you expect automatic cross-region failover (Redwood-managed) or a documented customer-driven failover playbook?

I am attaching an initial rider placeholder we use for enterprise pilots (QHP_Rider_InitialDraft_20260804.docx). It's intentionally conservative on credits and uses a regional fallback model.

If procurement is on a tight window, we can also provide a tracked-change PDF for quick review.

—Kimberly

Samir — quick technical proposal to seed the rider and Order Form exhibit. Below are suggested clauses; I've included a short redline PDF for the order-form paragraph (attached).

1) Uptime target (Order Form Exhibit A):
"Redwood will provide service availability of 99.95% measured monthly per REGION (US-EAST/US-WEST/EU-WEST). Availability excludes scheduled maintenance windows (we will provide >=72 hours notice) and force majeure events."

2) Latency SLOs (informational):
"95th percentile inference request latency (token generation API) for standard traffic <= 180ms p95; burst windows (defined in the exhibit) <= 350ms p95. Customers on dedicated capacity may set custom latency tiers via Order Form options."

3) Failover model:
"Redwood will maintain warm standby capacity in at least one alternative region. In the event of region-wide unavailability, Redwood will activate regional fallback within the operational window documented in the playbook. Activation is Redwood-managed for customers who opt into cross-region failover; customers may also select customer-managed failover from the provisioning options on the Order Form."

4) Escalation & notifications (short):
"Notification timeline: 15 minutes post-detection for Sev1 suspected outage; 1 hour for confirmed outage; 4 hours for interim root cause. Final RCA within 7 business days for Sev1 incidents. Contact list and paging details to be appended to Exhibit B (onboarding runbook)."

Attached: OrderForm_Exhibit_A_redline.pdf (contains inline tracked-change language for the Order Form paragraph and credits table).

If Quantum wants a single global SLA instead, we can collapse region-specific measurements into a consolidated availability metric — happy to provide both drafts.

Rishi
VP, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
Attachment: OrderForm_Exhibit_A_redline.pdf

Kimberly / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the two artifacts. The language in the OrderForm_Exhibit_A_redline.pdf looks good overall. A few small asks from legal/procurement:

- Please tighten the scheduled maintenance notice window to 48 hours when practical (we understand emergency patches may be shorter).
- Can the failover clause explicitly state that cross-region failover will not be invoked for performance degradation under 10% sustained error uplift? (We want to avoid unnecessary failovers).
- For the notification timeline, Quantum requires a customer-facing status page update within 30 minutes of detection in addition to the internal notifications.

If you can provide an updated PDF with those three small edits, we can route to our CFO and legal and aim to be back with signature comments by next Wednesday. After that we will need a DocuSign-ready Order Form + Exhibit.

Thanks,
Anna
